Published online:
September 8, 2026

Geographic focus:
Japan, USA, Singapore (global FX markets)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references August 2024 carry trade unwind as precedent
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ/Fed meetings the week of Sept 18 as key pivot
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural repricing of JPY carry trade, BOJ rate path through December and beyond

Synopsis:
The yen has surged sharply in early September 2026, hitting its strongest level since February at 152.89/USD, driven by near-certain BOJ rate hike expectations (97% probability of +25bps to 1.25%) and early signs of capital repatriation to Japan. This is triggering an accelerating unwind of the yen carry trade — estimated at a record ¥360 trillion ($2.35T) in cross-border borrowing. Unlike the disorderly 2024 unwind, markets are more prepared, but positioning remains large and a self-reinforcing unwind toward mid-140s USD/JPY is possible. Japan's 30-year high JGB yields mean capital no longer needs to leave Japan for returns. The September 18 BOJ decision is the key catalyst — if yen holds gains post-hike, it signals a genuine structural repricing of the carry trade.
